project_context.summary: Phase three of the East Bench House. The master bath floor is covered wall to wall in Schluter's button mat, the wire only runs where people stand, in front of the toilet, the vanity and the tub, and it runs on a programmable thermostat. Mike sets it to 85 and feels it through his socks.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short from 1:29 to 5:58, process in the middle, the finished bath at both ends.
notes: Never name the price in the Short, the long video carries it.

shorts.full_vo: This master bath has a heated tile floor, and here's how it goes in. First, the whole floor gets covered in a Schluter mat made for heated floors. All these little buttons hold the heating wire in place. The wire snaps in, and you run it wherever you want heat. I drew a map for my tile guy, and every yellow area gets heated. In front of the toilet, the vanity, and where you step out of the tub. Then thinset goes over the wire, and the tile sets right on top. Before any tile goes down, test the wire for continuity. Miss a break, and you find out after the tile is down. I turned it up to eighty-five. It's programmable, so the floor is warm before they're even out of bed.
shorts.voice_direction: Warm and practical, a contractor showing a friend the trick to a job he has done a hundred times.
